chapter: Life in France and Sidney Bechet
title: French fans, a French companion of fifteen years, and a failed French course
summary: Fans are surprised he speaks little French; he jokes about living fifteen years with a woman who spoke no English, tells a Claude Hopkins anecdote, and recalls quitting French lessons after three days.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Let me ask you another question. Have you found that you've made it clear that you're a resident of France, you've lived there practically 30 years, it'll be 30 years this December. Is there any resentment of your French fans of your not having a total assimilation of the French culture that - or do you think that they don't think about that at all? I mean are your French fans surprised if they come up to you for an autograph or something and they find that you're not strong in French?

Yeah, they're surprised at me because they know that I've been there 30 years (laughs). And they're - one guy says 'What, you've been here 30 years and you can't speak French?' 'Cause I got a little bit - I tell them I used to go with a French woman for 15 years - now this is something funny - I went with a woman for 15 years. We just, we still didn't fall out, we just -

Separated, you know, like one of those things. We're still friends, I mean her family's like brothers and sisters to me. And she lives, she can't live in Paris on account of the, she says her health, you know? So she has her own place down in the South of France. Except we were together 15 years. So when the people tell me, like 'You mean to say you can't speak French?' - I tell them, I said 'I must be speakin' something', I say, 'I live in a' - I don't know if I can say this on this thing or no -

I said "Actually I must be doing something". I said "I've been living with this woman for 15 years and she can't speak a word of English, see". So I told - I tell you who I told, told me that [ ], Claude Hopkins, when I was down at the, George Wein's festival in Nice, the second one, you know, they had that and I played the second and the third or somethin' like that, I played two times down there for George. And Claude Hopkins was down there, he's cross across, he says, could I introduce her to my friends. So Claude says "You can't speak French now, all these years you got" - I says "I must be speakin' something", I says "My friend right here, see, I've been together 15 years and I don't speak no English". Well, he says "Well, you don't have to speak no French for that" (PS laughs). Go say [to] Claude that you know me -
He worked here for you, didn't he?
He's been here many times. He's never worked the West End, he sat in a couple of times.
Yeah. But he still - matter of fact -

I'm ashamed of myself. I tell you what, I'm lazy there, see. But I'm not exactly, yeah, I'm not a lazy man. But I have so much work that I could go to school, you know, they don't cost that much because the school there is very, very cheap, that's - and I could go. But I, here's what happened - when I first went there I went to school and I paid - it's very cheap, too, I only paid 40 dollars, 40 francs or something like that, 40 francs - anyway it was very, very cheap at that period and I paid in advance, a month in advance. Only went three days (PS laughs). And matter of fact, that's the third day, I got a tour to go to Germany, see what I mean?
So when I come back I don't have no lessons, I paid my money out. So then I didn't do that no more. And I got these books and these records and I don't have this [ ] (laughs), but I can get by.
